Rewrite the proposed undo/redo design
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide describes AB3's undo/redo design, which refers to
the address book model and no longer matches TAssist.

Let's rewrite the proposal for TAssist snapshots, keeping undo/redo
optional and unimplemented, and replace the nine old diagrams with
three focused class, sequence, and activity diagrams.

commitResults.messageTitle: User Guide: Cover assignment commands in help
commitResults.messageBody:
The help section lists the topics in the command reference but leaves
out the assignment commands, which the reference already shows.

Let's mention them in the topic order and give a help assignment
example, so the guide matches the Help screen.

commitResults.messageTitle: Dispatch proposed undo and redo in TAssistParser
commitResults.messageBody:
The proposal registers undo and redo through CommandRegistry, which
only dispatches commands of the form "feature subcommand", so a
one-word undo would never reach its parser.

Let's have TAssistParser recognize them beside help, exit, and view.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check history requests before skipping the save
commitResults.messageBody:
LogicManager returns early when a command leaves the data unchanged.
An undo that only returns a history request would take that path, so
its snapshot would never be restored or saved.

Let's state that LogicManager checks for the request before that
return, matching the sequence diagram.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the undo/redo history as a composition
commitResults.messageBody:
The text says LogicManager owns its history, and the diagram's other
links already use composition, but the history link is a plain
association.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reword the undo sequence diagram precondition
commitResults.messageBody:
The note "startup data is not protected" reads as if the proposal
drops the startup protection that the text keeps.

Let's state the precondition instead: a previous entry exists and the
data file loaded, so saving is allowed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add participation set sequence diagram to DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The Participation commands section describes how participation set
works but has no diagram.

Let's add a sequence diagram showing how the command is parsed through
the command registry and how it replaces the student with an updated
copy in the active group.

commitResults.messageTitle: Split participation set diagram into two
commitResults.messageBody:
The diagram is 1806px wide, so the DG scales its labels far below the
body text, and it shows the internals of both the parser chain and the
model at once.

Let's move parsing into its own diagram, referenced from the execution
diagram through a ref frame, as the course DG tips suggest.

commitResults.messageTitle: Note the PlantUML lifeline limitation in DG
commitResults.messageBody:
PlantUML draws the ParticipationSetCommand lifeline past its destroy
marker. The DG already explains this limitation under the view and
undo diagrams.

Let's add the same note under the participation set diagram.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the saved result in participation set diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The diagram shows LogicManager returning the command's result r, but
after saving changed data, executeAndSave returns a copy of r marked
as saved.

Let's say so in the note and the final return label.

commitResults.messageTitle: Hold TAssist data in ModelManager
commitResults.messageBody:
Group, student, GUI and weekly-record features all need to reach the
TAssist data through the Model, but the Model only holds the
AddressBook.

Let's make ModelManager hold a copy of a TAssist beside the
AddressBook. Keep the AddressBook so existing commands keep working
until it is removed.

TAssist data is not saved yet, so the app starts with no groups.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let the Model manage tutorial groups
commitResults.messageBody:
Group commands need to add groups, look them up and switch the active
group, but the Model cannot do any of that yet.

Let's delegate these group operations from the Model to TAssist.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let the Model add and remove students in a group
commitResults.messageBody:
Student commands need to add students to a group and remove them, but
the Model cannot do that yet.

Let's delegate these student operations from the Model to TAssist.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep observable views of the active group
commitResults.messageBody:
The UI must show the active group and its students, and update them
as soon as either changes, but the Model offers no way to observe
them.

Let's expose the active group as a property, and the active group's
students as a list that follows whichever group is active.

commitResults.messageTitle: Expose the active group and its students to the UI
commitResults.messageBody:
The UI talks to Logic, not to the Model, so it cannot reach the new
active group views yet.

Let's add them to Logic so the GUI can show the active group and its
students.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe how the Model holds TAssist data in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide says the TAssist classes are not used by the app,
which is no longer true.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain how the UI observes the active group in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
Developers building the group, student and GUI features need to know
how the active group views stay up to date, and why they are built
this way.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the active group's name in the header
commitResults.messageBody:
The header always says the active group is "None", even though the
Model now knows which group is active.

Let's show the active group's name there, and update it whenever
another group becomes active. Long names are shortened, with the full
name in a tooltip.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a panel that lists the active group's students
commitResults.messageBody:
The Students screen should list the students of the active group, but
the only roster panel lists AddressBook contacts.

Let's add a panel that lists the active group's students by name and
student ID. When there is nothing to list, it says whether no group is
active or the active group has no students yet.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the active group's students on the Students screen
commitResults.messageBody:
The Students screen still lists AddressBook contacts, which TAssist
users do not manage.

Let's show the new student panel there instead, and remove the
contact roster. Contact commands keep working until AddressBook is
removed, but contacts are no longer shown.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the Students screen in the UG
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide says the Students screen lists contacts, which no longer
matches the app.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the student roster UI in the DG
commitResults.messageBody: The DG still describes the contact roster and its manual tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use one phrase when no group is active
commitResults.messageBody:
The header said "None", the Students screen said "No active group",
and the previews pointed to Students in their own words, so the same
state read differently in each place.

Let's say "No active group" everywhere, hide the "Active group"
caption when it would read twice, and drop the group caption on the
Students screen, as the header already names the group. Let's also
remove the extra line from the previews.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the tutorial groups in the group strip
commitResults.messageBody:
The strip below the header said "Tutorial groups coming soon", even
though the app now holds groups and knows which one is active.

Let's show a chip for each group there, as in the UI mock-up, and
highlight the active one. When there are no groups, the strip says so.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the current screen after contact commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Contact commands switch to the Students screen, which no longer shows
contacts, so the user sees nothing happen.

Let's keep the current screen after any command that does not ask for
a screen. Contact commands still report their result in the feedback
box until AddressBook is removed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show help only on the Help screen
commitResults.messageBody:
help printed the command reference into the small feedback box, while
F1, the menu and view help showed the same reference on the Help
screen. The feedback box fits only a few lines, so the reference there
was hard to read.

Let's make help open the Help screen and only confirm in the feedback
box. help TOPIC opens the Help screen at that topic's commands. The
help text formatter is no longer used, so let's remove it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fit the feedback box to its message
commitResults.messageBody:
The feedback box was fixed at 62 to 90 pixels, so a message with a
command's usage showed two lines and a scroll bar. Feedback is how
users learn whether a command worked, so it should be readable at a
glance.

Let's grow the box with its message, from one line up to six. Only
longer messages scroll, and short ones leave more room for the screen
above.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the reworked workspace in the UG and DG
commitResults.messageBody:

box, contact commands opening Students, and no group strip.

The Help screen listed feature commands in alphabetical order of their

Let's group feature commands by topic in the order of the help topics.

commitResults.messageTitle: List each topic's commands in the order they are used
commitResults.messageBody:
Within a topic, help listed commands alphabetically, so student delete
came before student list and attendance list before attendance mark.
The User Guide describes them in the order a TA uses them.

Let's keep help entries in registration order, and register each
feature's commands in that order: create or record first, then list,
then delete.

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct the help text of the built-in commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The help entry still said help shows only one topic, although help
TOPIC now opens the reference at that topic. The general commands were
also headed "Current commands", a leftover from the contact commands.

Let's describe help, view and exit as they behave now, list the help
topics, and head the general commands "General commands".

commitResults.messageTitle: Complete the help for group and student commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The group help did not give the naming rules, and its group use example
switched to T02, which the examples never create. The student delete
example removed Alice Tan, whom the attendance and participation
examples go on to use.

Let's state the rules of each command, and give examples that work
when typed in order: create T01 and T02, switch back to T01, add two
students, and delete only the second.

commitResults.messageTitle: Complete the help for attendance and participation
commitResults.messageBody:
The attendance help did not say that IDs and statuses ignore case, or
what attendance list shows when no one has a mark that week. Weeks were
written as "week 1-13" in one place and "a week from 1 to 13" in
another.

Let's state these rules as the User Guide does, in the same words for
both features.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check that every help example works when typed
commitResults.messageBody:
The help promises examples a TA can type, but nothing checked that
they run, so an example could fail without anyone noticing.

Let's test the running app's help: it lists every command in help
order, each example runs its own command, and typing every example in
order into a new TAssist succeeds.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make the User Guide and help agree
commitResults.messageBody:
The User Guide described the student commands after attendance and
participation, while help lists them right after the group commands.
Several help examples, such as group add g/T02 and the student delete
example, did not appear in the guide at all.

Let's order the guide's sections as help does, show every help example
in the guide, explain how the Help screen is ordered, and test that the
guide shows every help format and example.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain how help is ordered and checked in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
Developers adding commands, such as the assignment commands, need to
know where their help appears, what makes a good example, and which
test will fail if help and the User Guide disagree.

Let's describe the order of the reference and the rules for help text,
with a class diagram of how help entries reach the Help screen.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a TAssist icon for the app window
commitResults.messageBody:
The window and task bar show AddressBook's icon, which is not ours and
does not match TAssist.

Let's draw a TAssist icon, a white T with a check mark on the app's
teal, and use it in 32 and 256 pixel sizes so that the platform can
pick a sharp one. Let's remove the AddressBook icon and its entry in
copyright.txt, and credit the new icon there.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the TAssist icon in the macOS Dock
commitResults.messageBody:
JavaFX window icons do not reach the macOS Dock, which keeps showing
the Java icon. Windows and Linux take the task bar icon from the
window, so only macOS is affected.

Let's also set the icon through the Java platform's Taskbar where it
supports icon images. Where it does not, or the image cannot be read,
log it and carry on, as the icon is not essential.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say that a mark replaces only that student's week
commitResults.messageBody:
The help said marking or setting "the same week again" replaces the
earlier record, which can be read as a later week 3 mark replacing
another student's week 3 mark.

Let's say "the same student and week", as the User Guide does.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match the User Guide samples to the help session
commitResults.messageBody:
After the help examples delete Ben Lim, the attendance and
participation list samples still showed him as Not recorded. The
command summary also kept group use g/T02 and the old student delete
example, which no longer follow on from the other examples.

Let's show only Alice Tan in those samples, use the help examples in
the command summary, and test that the summary uses only help
examples.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep starting if the Dock icon cannot be set
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskbarIcon caught only some of the exceptions that setting the icon
can throw. On macOS, a failure to set the Dock icon arrives as a plain
RuntimeException, and UiManager calls TaskbarIcon outside its own
error handling, so such a failure would stop TAssist from starting.

Let's catch any RuntimeException there, log it, and carry on without
the Dock icon.

commitResults.messageTitle: Read the Dock icon before checking platform support
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskbarIcon returned as soon as the platform did not support task bar
icons, before looking at the image. On headless CI that is always the
case, so the tests for a missing or unreadable image passed without
ever reading it.

Let's read the image first, in its own method, and test that method
directly with the real icon, a missing file and a file that is not an
image.

commitResults.messageBody:
Each tutorial group in the data file holds its name and its students.
A manual edit may leave out the student list, add an empty entry, or
repeat a student ID within the group.

Let's add a Jackson-friendly group that reads a missing student list as
no students, and rejects empty entries and repeated student IDs with a
message naming the group.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a JSON form of the whole TAssist data
commitResults.messageBody:
The data file holds every tutorial group and which group is active. A
manual edit may repeat a group name in a different case, name an active
group that does not exist, or leave out either field.

Let's add a serializable TAssist that reads a missing group list as no
groups and a missing active group as none, and rejects repeated group
names and an unknown active group with a specific message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JSON file storage for TAssist data
commitResults.messageBody:
TAssist data lives only in memory, so tutorial groups and students are
lost when the app closes.

Let's add a storage class that saves TAssist data to a JSON file and
reads it back, reporting a missing file as no data and an unreadable or
invalid file as a loading error.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let Storage read and save TAssist data
commitResults.messageBody:
The JSON storage for TAssist data is not reachable through the Storage
component, so Logic and the app launcher cannot use it.

Let's give Storage methods to read and save TAssist data, and keep the
TAssist data file at data/tassist.json.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save TAssist data after each command
commitResults.messageBody:
Successful commands save AddressBook data, so changes to tutorial
groups, students and the active group are lost when the app closes.

Let's save TAssist data instead, so the data file follows every
successful command other than view. A failed save is still reported to
the user.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load TAssist data from the data file at startup
commitResults.messageBody:
Every run starts with no tutorial groups, and a first launch fills the
app with sample contacts.

Let's restore groups, students and the active group from the TAssist
data file when the app starts. A missing file starts an empty TAssist
with no sample data, and an unreadable or invalid file starts an empty
TAssist and logs why the file could not be read. AddressBook data is no
longer loaded.

commitResults.messageTitle: Stop wiring AddressBook storage into Storage
commitResults.messageBody:
The app no longer reads or saves AddressBook data, so the AddressBook
methods of Storage are unused.

Let's remove them from Storage and StorageManager. The AddressBook
storage classes stay until the AddressBook code is removed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe TAssist data on the Storage screen
commitResults.messageBody:
The Storage screen says contact commands are saved and a first launch
shows sample contacts, which is no longer true.

Let's say that tutorial groups and students are saved and that a first
launch starts empty.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the TAssist data file in the UG
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG says contact data is saved to data/addressbook.json and that a
first launch shows sample data, which is no longer true.

Let's describe what TAssist saves, where the data file is, what it
looks like, and what happens when it is missing or invalid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show TAssist storage in the storage class diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The storage class diagram shows AddressBook storage, which Storage no
longer uses.

Let's show the TAssist storage classes in its place.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe saving and loading TAssist data in the DG
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG says TAssist data is not saved and describes AddressBook
storage, and its manual tests expect sample contacts on first launch.

Let's describe the TAssist data file, how it is saved and loaded, how
later features add their own records to it, and how to test a missing
or invalid file by hand.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test loading TAssist data at startup
commitResults.messageBody:
Loading the data file at startup has no tests, so a regression in how
a missing, valid or invalid file is handled would go unnoticed.

Let's make the model setup in MainApp visible to tests in its package,
and test each of the three cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject a data file that holds only null
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file whose whole content is null makes JsonUtil return
Optional.of(null), which throws NullPointerException and crashes the
app at startup instead of starting with an empty TAssist.

Let's treat such a file as unreadable, so it is reported like any other
invalid file. This also covers the preferences file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Quote the active group name in load errors
commitResults.messageBody:
When the active group in the data file is blank, the error reads "The
active group  is not in the group list.", which hides what is wrong.

Let's quote the name, so a blank or space-padded name is visible.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tidy TAssist storage Javadoc and message names
commitResults.messageBody:
One saveTAssist overload documents only one of its two parameters, and
the group adapter names its missing-field message differently from the
student adapter.

Let's document both parameters and use the student adapter's naming
for the group's missing-field message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check why rejected TAssist files are rejected
commitResults.messageBody:
Some storage tests only check that an invalid file is rejected, so they
would still pass if it were rejected for the wrong reason.

Let's also check the reason, and name the active group test after both
things it covers.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mention the active group on the Storage screen
commitResults.messageBody:
The Storage screen lists tutorial groups and students as saved data,
but the active group is saved too.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify failed commands and contacts in the docs
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG says a failed command does not change data, but a command whose
save fails has already changed the data in memory. The DG paragraph on
contact commands does not say that contacts are no longer saved.

Let's restore the UG's earlier wording about failed commands, and say
in the DG that contacts are not saved.

commitResults.messageTitle: Title the student card with the group name
commitResults.messageBody:
The card said "Student roster" and showed the count at the far right,
repeating the Students tab and the active group shown elsewhere. Title
it with the group name and a count badge instead.

Show the empty state in place of the table, so that column headings
no longer sit above an explanation, and center its text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge the header and group strip into one top bar
commitResults.messageBody:
The dark header and the group strip took two rows, and the active group
appeared in the header, the strip and the student card. Replace them
with one light bar that holds the brand, the group chips and a Help
button.

The menu bar is removed. Help stays on F1, the Help button and the help
command, and the window can still be closed or exited with exit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Open screens from a navigation bar
commitResults.messageBody:
The tab strip gave all seven screens equal weight, including four that
are still previews, and Help and Storage looked like data screens.

Hide the tab strip and open the screens from a bar in the top chrome:
the screens that hold group data come first, and Groups, Help and
Storage sit at the right. A dot marks a screen that is still a preview.
Each tooltip names the equivalent view command, and clicking keeps the
keyboard focus in the command box.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mark command feedback with a state icon
commitResults.messageBody:
The feedback was a mint box that only turned pink on failure. Show a
check or a cross beside the message on a white row, and tint the row
only for failures.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show shortcuts in the footer and tidy the student table
commitResults.messageBody:
The "Enter" hint in the command box told the user nothing new. Put the
F1 and Esc shortcuts in the footer instead, and show the command box
border at full strength only while it has focus.

Give the student table fixed column widths, so that a student ID sits
beside the name on wide windows, and let the row dividers span the
whole table.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the reworked top bar and feedback in the docs
commitResults.messageBody:
Update the User Guide, the Developer Guide and the UI class diagram for
the navigation bar, the group chips in the top bar, the feedback icon
and the footer shortcuts.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the footer status dot visible in narrow windows
commitResults.messageBody:
The dot shrank to an ellipsis at the minimum window width. Also render
that width in the UI smoke test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mark a failed command in the footer
commitResults.messageBody:
The footer said "Command failed" beside the same green dot as a
success. Turn the dot red for a failed command, so that the two cases
differ at a glance.

commitResults.messageTitle: Center the feedback row and enlarge the failure icon
commitResults.messageBody:
A one-line message sat a few pixels above the middle of its row, and
the cross in a failure looked smaller than the check mark. Drop the
text area's own padding, rebalance the row padding, and enlarge the
cross.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say that the GUI is adapted from the mockup
commitResults.messageBody:
The Acknowledgements and the style sheet said that the GUI follows the
team-supplied mockup. The top bar and the navigation bar now differ from
it, so say that the design is based on the mockup and name what is
different.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the real UI on the home page and README
commitResults.messageBody:
Ui.png was the team's mock-up, which shows features that do not exist
yet and the old dark header. Replace it with a screenshot of the
implemented GUI.

Keep the mock-up as UiMockup.png and link it from the Developer Guide,
so that it stays in the repository as the design reference.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the User Guide screenshot
commitResults.messageBody:
The screenshot showed the contact roster and the old header. Show the
GUI as it appears on the first launch, as the Quick Start describes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct the help and navigation descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide still said that HelpCommand formats the entries with
HelpCatalog.format, which no longer exists, and that a navigation button
does everything view SCREEN does, although it does not show the feedback
message. Describe what the code does.

Also rename the stale v1.2 testing heading and drop the unused
card-caption style.

The add, edit, delete, clear, find and list commands only work on the

- Drop their help entries so help only lists view, help and exit

commitResults.messageBody:
Nothing reads or writes the AddressBook data file now that TAssist has
its own data file.

- Delete JsonAddressBookStorage and JsonSerializableAddressBook
- Delete their tests and test data files

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove the address book from Model and Logic
commitResults.messageBody:
The Model and Logic APIs still carried the person list, which no
command or screen uses now that TAssist holds the groups and students.

- Drop the person methods and filter predicate from Model and
  ModelManager, which now takes TAssist data and user prefs only
- Drop getFilteredPersonList from Logic and LogicManager
- Start MainApp with the loaded TAssist data and nothing else
- Update the model, logic and UI tests to match

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove person parsing helpers and messages
commitResults.messageBody:
ParserUtil and Messages still held parsing and display code for the
AddressBook person fields, which no command uses.

- Keep ParserUtil.parseIndex, the only helper that is not person based
- Keep the duplicate prefix message used by the argument parsers

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove the person and tag model
commitResults.messageBody:
No code uses the AddressBook person, its fields, tags or sample data
now that commands, storage and the Model no longer refer to them.

- Delete AddressBook, ReadOnlyAddressBook, the person and tag packages,
  SampleDataUtil, JsonAdaptedPerson, JsonAdaptedTag and CliSyntax
- Delete their tests, test builders and typical person fixtures
- Drop the person constants from CommandTestUtil

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename AddressBookParser to TAssistParser
commitResults.messageBody:
The class no longer parses anything from AddressBook, and its name is
shown in logs and docs.

- Rename AddressBookParser and its test to TAssistParser
- Say which commands a feature keyword must not clash with

commitResults.messageTitle: Show TAssist instead of AddressBook in messages
commitResults.messageBody:
The exit message and the startup and shutdown logs still named the
AddressBook app.

- Say "Exiting TAssist" when the user enters exit
- Name TAssist in the MainApp log lines
- Reword a MainWindow comment that mentioned contacts

commitResults.messageTitle: User Guide: remove the AddressBook commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The add, list, edit, find, delete and clear commands no longer exist,
so the User Guide must not describe them.

- Remove their sections, the command summary rows and the note that

- Use help, view and exit in the quick start and the format notes
- Delete the find command screenshot

commitResults.messageTitle: Developer Guide: update for the removed AddressBook
commitResults.messageBody:
The Design section, diagrams and manual tests still described the

- Drop the AddressBook and person text, the alternative model diagram

- Call the parser TAssistParser and list help, view and exit as the

commitResults.messageTitle: LogicManagerTest: add the parsed student

The registered command test parsed the name and ID but added a fixed
student, so it did not show that parsing reaches the model.

- Build the student from the parsed values
- Expect the whitespace-normalized name in the model

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove unused AB3 index and tokenizer classes
commitResults.messageBody:
Nothing in TAssist calls them now that the AddressBook commands are
gone: TAssistArgumentParser tokenizes its own arguments and commands
identify students by student ID instead of a list index.

- Delete ArgumentTokenizer, ParserUtil and Index with their tests

commitResults.messageTitle: Use "built-in" for the help, view and exit commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Only three general commands are left, so calling them "legacy" no
longer describes them, and a few comments still mention the removed
filter and AddressBook.

- Rename the legacy constants, comments and tests to built-in
- Drop the filter from the ViewCommand and Developer Guide wording
- Say TAssist's architecture in SettingUp.md

commitResults.messageBody:
No page of the User Guide or Developer Guide refers to them, and they

- Delete the unreferenced helpMessage and LogicStorageDIP images

The built JAR was still called addressbook.jar and the log file

- Build build/libs/tassist.jar and write tassist.log
- Update the User Guide, DevOps guide and AGENTS.md to match

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept startup file paths in MainApp
commitResults.messageBody:
init() always reads preferences.json and data/tassist.json, so a
test cannot start the app without touching the real files.

Let a package-private constructor supply those paths. The public
constructor still uses the same default files.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test MainApp startup and shutdown
commitResults.messageBody:
The TAssist startup, UI start and shutdown log lines in MainApp are

- Check that stop writes the user preferences

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep saved files inside the JAR folder
commitResults.messageBody:
TAssist writes preferences, data, and logs relative to the
working directory. Launching the JAR from another folder
therefore creates files outside the folder that contains the
JAR, which breaks the data-sandbox constraint.

Save those files in the JAR's folder instead. When the app is
not running from a JAR, keep using the working directory.

The User Guide still describes AddressBook data archiving as
coming in v2.0. TAssist has no archiving command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assignments to the model
commitResults.messageBody:
A group has no way to hold the assignments the TA creates for it.

Add Assignment, AssignmentName and UniqueAssignmentList, modelled on
Group, GroupName and UniqueGroupList. Names allow 1-60 letters, digits,
spaces and hyphens and are unique within a group, ignoring case.

Let Group hold its assignments and add Model#addAssignment so commands
change a group through the model, as they do for students.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save assignments in the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
Assignments created for a group are lost when the app is closed.

Add an optional assignments list of names to each group in the data
file. A missing list loads as no assignments, so existing files still
open. Reject an invalid, empty or duplicate name with a message that
says what is wrong, so a wrong manual edit does not crash the app.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assignment add command
commitResults.messageBody:
A TA cannot create the assignments of a tutorial group.

Add "assignment add a/ASSIGNMENT_NAME", which creates an assignment in
the active group and rejects a name that already exists there, ignoring
case. Parse assignment names with the same rules as the model, so an
invalid name is reported as a constraint error.

The command is wired into the app in a later commit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assignment list command
commitResults.messageBody:
A TA cannot see which students have handed in an assignment.

Add "assignment list a/ASSIGNMENT_NAME", which shows every student of
the active group in roster order with their submission status and
grade, for example "Alice Tan | A0123456X | Not submitted | -". No
submission or grade can be recorded yet, so every row shows the default.

Report an unknown assignment with a message that names the group and
how to create the assignment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Register assignment commands in the app
commitResults.messageBody:
The assignment commands cannot be typed until they are registered.

Register "assignment add" and "assignment list" with their help
entries at startup, so they appear in the command reference and in
"help assignment". Cover the commands end to end, including saving and
reopening the app and rejected input leaving the data file unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document assignments in the User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Users cannot learn how to create assignments or list their records.

Describe "assignment add" and "assignment list" with their naming
rules, sample output and error messages. Add the assignments list to
the data file description and the command summary, and say that
commands for submissions and grades are still to come.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document assignments in the Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The design of the assignment feature is not recorded.

Describe how the assignment commands, model and data file work, and
that every record shows the default status until submissions can be
recorded. Update the validation rules, the model diagram and the
manual testing steps to match.
